message.content:
**Hydrogen – A Quick Reference to Its Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| | Natural abundance | ¹H ≈ 99.98 %, ²H ≈ 0.02 %, ³H negligible |
| **Physical State (Room Temp.)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (≈ 0.0000899 g cm⁻³) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Vapor pressure | 1 atm at 20.28 K |
| | Specific heat (gas, 1 bar) | 28.8 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat of fusion | 0.001 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Properties** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy (1st) | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative → energy released when H⁻ forms) |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Acidic behavior | Acts as a proton donor (H⁺) in aqueous solution |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydride ions (H⁻) in metal hydrides |
| | Redox behavior | Strong reducing agent (e.g., H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻) |
| **Molecular Properties** | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Dipole moment (H₂) | 0 (homonuclear diatomic) |
| | Rotational constant | 60.853 cm⁻¹ |
| | Vibrational frequency | 4401 cm⁻¹ (fundamental) |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman, Balmer series (visible) |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Deuterium (²H) | 2.014 u, heavier, lower zero‑point energy, used in heavy water (D₂O) |
| | Tritium (³H) | 3.016 u, radioactive (β⁻ decay, half‑life 12.32 y) |
| | Applications | Tracer studies, nuclear fusion (DT reaction), heavy‑water reactors |
| **Miscellaneous** | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_B (proton) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard entropy (gas) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |

---

### Quick Takeaways

1. **Lightest Element** – Hydrogen is the simplest atom, with only one proton and one electron.
2. **Highly Reactive** – It readily forms covalent bonds (H₂) or ionic bonds (hydrides, acids).
3. **Low Density & Low Boiling Point** – Makes it a gas under most Earth conditions.
4. **Isotopic Diversity** – Protium, deuterium, and tritium give hydrogen unique roles in chemistry, physics, and energy research.
5. **Key Role in Life & Energy** – From water to fuels (methane, ammonia) to fusion research.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
